slot.brief: Use T² ∝ a³ to find the orbital period (or semi-major axis) of a planet compared to that of Earth.

stem: A planet orbiting the Sun has a semi-major axis of $4$ AU. What is its orbital period in Earth years?

verdicts.working: By Kepler’s third law, P² = a³ in Earth years and AU. Thus P = √(4³) = 8 years.

working:
$\dfrac{T^2}{T_E^2}=\left(\dfrac{a}{a_E}\right)^3$; $T_E=1$ year, $a_E=1$ AU.
$T^2=4^3=64\ \text{years}^2 \Rightarrow T=8$ years.

Independent check: By Kepler’s third law, P² = a³ in Earth years and AU. Thus P = √(4³) = 8 years.
solution:
By Kepler’s third law, $T^2/T_E^2=(a/a_E)^3$. With $T_E=1$ year, $a_E=1$ AU, and $a=4$ AU,
$$T^2=4^3=64 \quad\Rightarrow\quad T=8\text{ years}.$$
